about: The ADR-187 divergence ledger for SCALPEL (ADR-187 §5, started by ADR-189 / B355). Every intentional difference between the parity target (the composed engine) and an oracle it calls (the SCALPEL oracle; since B382 also SwarmSynth, reference/swarmsaw.html), one entry each; the order of the entries carries no meaning. A built entry sits behind its own engine flag, default 0 unless the entry says `default: 1` (B382, ADR-187 A1: a divergence the human ruled ON, one per PR; it carries `ruled`, and `moves` for each pinned scenario it changes at the defaults), so all flags off is the engine before the first divergence, bit for bit. Checked by tools/labharness/divergence_ledger_check.mjs (./verify fast): L1 shape, L2 the oracle blob, L3 each built flag exists at its ledgered default, L4 all off = the pinned fingerprints below and the defaults = the pins or the claimed moves, L5 each built flag changes a scenario, L6 each stays in its declared scope. Mirror policy (ADR-187, ratified): the composed engine IS the lab JS, so these are mirrored by construction; js_limit states what the browser cannot follow, or null.

allOff.about: Fingerprints of the composed engine BEFORE B355 (main at d443eb6, the engine at blob 5f96285): each preset from reference/scalpel/data/presets.json, notes 57 and 64 struck at 0, 12032 samples at 48 kHz in 128-sample blocks, Math.random seeded mulberry32(seed); SHA-256 of the float32 L then R, first 16 hex digits (divergence_ledger_check.mjs fingerprint()).
allOff.pinSets: Two pin sets, on purpose: these (divergence_ledger_check.mjs fingerprint(): notes 57 + 64 at 0, 12032 samples, seed 45909) and composed_engine_check AA0 (its renderWith: two notes and a release, 24064 samples, seed 0xB355), both taken on main d443eb6. Zap bass joined both in the B355 rework: after ADR-189 A1 narrowed D1, no other pinned preset is inside D1's scope.

metricSuite: B346's estimator as merged on main (PR #847, merge 9529eae): tools/patchspace/alias_sources.mjs estimate() over metrics.mjs aliasConvergence, totalDb against an oversampled truth (8N and 16N, the output stage done right). Each flag is judged against the ENGINE-AS-IS truth (B346's rule) and against its OWN truth. Populations: B346's 34 rated patches x A1/E5/A5 (the 72 with as-is total > -60 dB); the 83 bench presets x A1/E5/A5 (186 of 249 over -60 dB); the 83 bench presets with Band-limit OFF (no bench preset has it off; 220 of 249). helped = the total falls 3 dB or more, worse = it rises 3 dB or more. The B355 rework trace has the runs.

divergences.description: First-order ADAA on a blade carrier, REPLACING the scanner's carrier-wrap PolyBLEPs, NARROWED by ADR-189 A1 to where it beats them: the carrier shape is not sine (nor sine->saw, which has no antiderivative), AND (the blade is an FM mode, 1 or 2, OR Band-limit is off), AND an FM blade's modulator is not S&H (mshape 7). Discrete per-blade parameters, no thresholds. Everywhere else the carrier keeps its BLEPs, bit for bit. The carrier sample becomes its mean over the phase swept since the previous internal sample, (F(cp) - F(cp0))/(cp - cp0) with the oracle's RazorCore.F; the midpoint below |cp - cp0| < 1e-7; the plain sample at blade entry. Half an internal sample of carrier-content lag, uncompensated (the engine header states why).

oracle.sites: voice() :187, :192, :200 (the carrier sample); scan() :613-617 (the carrier-wrap BLEPs)

divergences.scope: blade carriers with a non-sine shape in FM modes (1, 2) without an S&H modulator, and every non-sine carrier (sync, FM, ring) when Band-limit is off; 5 of the 83 bench presets as shipped (Trance jitter, Zap bass, Jitter swarm, Frozen noise FM, Operator jitter)

divergences.finding: As first built (every carrier), D1 made plain sync and ring carriers with Band-limit on WORSE than the PolyBLEP it replaced (a periodic sync saw's inharmonic residual -30.3 -> -22.8 dB; the bench: 30 helped, 66 worse over 182, the critic), and S&H-modulated FM carriers worse (the mean smears the phase jumps). A1 narrowed it; after: bench 13 helped / 0 worse, rated 72 8 / 0, Band-limit off 102 / 0, each against the as-is truth. A second mechanism the critic found, moot for the narrowed scope but recorded: at a blade EDGE, entry returns the plain sample and then switches to the half-sample-lagged mean, while the edge BLEP heights come from the plain voice (hAt); on sine carriers (now excluded) that mismatch made edges worse.
divergences.note: JS-only mechanism (static voice swap): a subclass cannot reach the static voice() that out()/outSerial() call by name, so the lab swaps RazorCore.voice for the render. The C++ implements the carrier AA choice inline in voice() as per-instance state; the swap is not part of the divergence.

divergences.description: The onset lock (a note-start coupling burst, Kenv, decaying over dissolve) is BIPOLAR, the C++'s law (ADR-056): Kenv = 8*onset*|onset|, its positive part added to the sync target and 3x its negative part to the splay target (the x3 of the steady splay gain), so a negative onset is a SPLAY burst. SwarmSynth squares the sign away (Kenv = 8*onset^2), so onset -x played the same sync burst as +x, although the composed engine exposes onset -1..1. For onset >= 0 both laws are the same expressions (ADR-056's superset proof), so nothing there moves. Built as a text patch of SwarmSynth's noteOn and controlTick (the engine's SWARM_PATCHES); 0 is SwarmSynth's expression, character for character.

divergences.description: The PolyBLEP scanner tracks the xin phase input (feedback and cross-member modulation): the step's xin is added to the carrier phase the scanner interpolates, at both ends (B346's blepXin; the BLEP height probe reads the current xin, so the previous-xin form places edges the probe cannot see). Carriers only (a crush step does not move with xin).

divergences.description: Detune law 3 is the C++'s TEMPO GRID (ADR-022): cents placement, then each member's Hz offset from the pitch snapped to the nearest multiple of u = (bpm/60)*beatMult (rounding half away from zero, std::round's rule), so every pairwise beat rate is an exact multiple of the grid; drift, after, loosens it as in the C++. SwarmSynth has no law 3 and falls through to ERB. bpm and beatMult are new engine keys at the C++'s Params defaults (120, 1); the plugin takes bpm from the host transport, the lab has none. The lab's law menu does not offer 3 (critic L6 on B379), but saved state, automation and set() can carry one. Built as a text patch of SwarmSynth's controlTick law chain (the engine's SWARM_PATCHES); 0 is SwarmSynth's ERB fall-through, and no other law is touched.

divergences.description: The feedback / cross-mod loop keeps the ORACLE'S TAP (the PolyBLEP output, render :840) and runs it through a one-pole low-pass at 5 kHz (LOOP_FC; a time constant in seconds, converted per internal sample). ADR-189 A1: the tap change first built (tapping the current sample) was DROPPED: it moved broad#828's rate-locked cycle from R/5 to R/3 instead of curing it, and made broad#857 A5 6.2 dB worse. Measured on broad#828 A1/E5 at os 1/2/4/8, the worst line over its local floor: off +19.4, 3 kHz +2.3, 4 kHz +1.3, 5 kHz +2.2, 6 kHz +3.4, 8 kHz +7.1; broad#540 (the other patch with the cycle): off +20.2, 4 kHz +1.6, 5 kHz +3.0. 5 kHz is the highest cutoff with every line within the +-3 dB scatter of a clean reference. Halving or quartering the loop gain leaves the cycle; os only moves it. The oracle's xin is overwritten in stepM before the blade step reads it.

divergences.finding: Final form (ADR-189 A1): the oracle's tap + a 5 kHz one-pole loop filter. broad#828's R/5 line reads -5.9 dB over its floor with D3 at os 1 (+13.0 without; composed_engine_check AA3). Audible cost, a 1 s held note, the largest 1/3-octave band change within 40 dB of the peak: Feedback choir -21.6 dB at 16 kHz (A3; its truth-to-truth timbre change there is -23.7, and its aliasing falls -14.0 -> -67.1 dB), Feedback screech -14.9 at 16 kHz, Cross-mod ring (watch) -11.7 at 16 kHz, Screamer +9.7 at 12.8 kHz, Feedback snarl +9.5 at 1.6 kHz (E5); level changes are 1.1 dB or less. Every preset without feedback or cross-mod is bit-identical (L6). The first form's figures (the moved tap + 3 kHz; 'Feedback choir -30.7 dB at 16 kHz', the critic's measure of it) are superseded.

divergences.description: The coupling smoother's per-tick coefficient comes from a time constant in SECONDS, B150's law in the C++ (SwarmCore(): 0.08 at 44.1 kHz exactly, else 1 - exp(-(16/sr)/kKsmTauSeconds), kKsmTauSeconds = 4.3512 ms, the value that gives 0.08 at 44.1 kHz), in place of SwarmSynth's literal 0.08 per 16-sample tick at every rate (an ADR-009 per-tick constant: 4.35 ms at 44.1 kHz, 4.00 ms at 48 kHz, 2.00 ms at 96 kHz). Resolved once per SwarmSynth, at construction, as the C++ does. 44.1 kHz is special-cased to the literal, as in the C++, because the round trip is three ULP short of 0.08. 48 kHz: 0.073746064208033535. Built as a text patch of SwarmSynth's constructor and controlTick (the engine's SWARM_PATCHES); 0 is SwarmSynth's expression, character for character.

divergences.finding: (1) The 48 kHz golden set (B382) tested B379's hypothesis 'M1 and M2 are the only 48 kHz differences' on the whole L0-1 matrix: with M1 mirrored, every SwarmSynth scenario is within 1e-6 of the C++; the only other differences are negative onset (M2) and law 3 (M3), and DynSynth (reference/swarmdynamics.html) carries the SAME per-tick 0.08 in its own smoother (controlTick, s.Ksm): with it replaced by M1's coefficient every dyn scenario is within 1e-6 of the C++, without it 21 of 24 miss by 4e-5 to 9e-2 (dyn-grid, K 0, does not). That is a fact about the reference the C++ parity chain was built on, not an engine divergence (the composed engine runs none of DynSynth's coupling). (2) broad#828, AA3's evidence for D3: at the defaults (M1 on) its R/5 limit cycle at E5, os 1, reads +2.3 dB over its floor, not +13.0 (D3 on: -0.6, not -5.9): the cycle depends on the swarm's realisation. AA3 keeps M1 off, the swarm the cycle was measured on. (3) Crunch horde at the defaults is PLATFORM-FRAGILE: 57a4d13ff66d7a9f on macOS, f07ffc9432bcb49d on CI Linux (PR #880, run 36782771270). On macOS those are the two outcomes of perturbing the swarm by ~1e-12 relative (M1's coefficient moved +1e5 ULP gives exactly the Linux hash; +-1 to +-1e4 ULP change nothing), so a last-bit difference somewhere upstream, NOT M1's coefficient, picks the side; its pin is per platform (divergence_ledger_check PER-PLATFORM PINS). Cross-mod roar and Zap bass matched on Linux.

divergences.description: The random-patch sampler weights Band-limit toward ON, versioned so the committed listening sample still reproduces. A patch-space change, not an engine one: listed here so every ADR-189 divergence is in one place.
